item: The Ed25519 evidence key is wrapped under the held passphrase, created 0600 from its first byte, and made once (E3 / A-009, R442)
summary: On a store with a passphrase held (OO_KEY_PASSPHRASE, else the database passphrase: the custody signer's own helper) the evidence key file is the custody signer's wrap of the 32 key bytes (scrypt N=2^15, AES-256-GCM; not a PKCS8 PEM, whose PBKDF2 at 2048 rounds would make the file a 0.3 ms-a-guess oracle for the database passphrase), so a copied data folder no longer lets its holder sign as this install; before, it was written with NoEncryption whatever the store. It is created with os.open O_EXCL at mode 0600 from the first byte (the old write then chmod left a 0644 moment under umask 022) and linked into place from a finished private copy kept under keys/.pending/ (never a temporary name two callers share, and not in the listing a backup takes), so two first callers end with ONE key (the old code let both write and the last win after the first had signed) and no reader sees a half-written file. A key written before is wrapped IN PLACE the first time it is loaded under a passphrase: the same key (a new one would orphan every signed bundle), written to a sibling file, read back and compared before it replaces anything, and a failed wrap leaves the original and logs only the exception class. A wrapped key that cannot be opened (no passphrase held, or another install's) raises EvidenceKeyError (a ValueError, so the evidence route still answers 409) naming the cause, and nothing is ever regenerated or overwritten; the review readers read with the held passphrase and never write or wrap. No recovery for a lost passphrase (R442 d); a restore brings the key as the source install wrapped it, exactly like the custody key (R442 b), and an evidence export and every backup then refuse with the cause until the file is moved aside (re-wrapping inside the restore is a proposal for src/backup/merge.py). Left, named: the custody Ed25519 key is still a PKCS8 PEM under BestAvailableEncryption (2048 PBKDF2 rounds: the cheap oracle remains there), its write-then-chmod create in src/custody/signing.py, and the keys_destroyed tally in src/safety/crypto_erase.py.
